correctness.rationale: For an independent set meeting both sides, crown adjacency confines it to one deleted matched pair. For a set of size s inside one side, opposite-side vertices see s-1 or s selected neighbors; for 1<s<n both positive consecutive values occur, and for s=n the value n-1 is even because n is odd. Hence alpha_od=2 and the only maxima are deleted pairs. Strong odd color classes are odd independent sets, giving chi_so>=n; the deleted-pair partition gives n colors and forces uniqueness at equality. The bundled exact checker independently verifies definitions for n=3,5,7,9.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard, highly symmetric bipartite family, and the initiating paper explicitly develops odd independence alongside strong odd coloring and highlights the product inequality as fundamental. The result gives an exact infinite even-degree regular-bipartite family in which the general even-degree bound is far from the true value, classifies all maxima and all optimal colorings, and supplies a new equality family for alpha_od(G) chi_so(G) >= |G|. This is structural rather than a parameter substitution or finite-table recomputation.
